Analysis complete under your conditions. Seed = 20261023 everywhere; unit of inference = plot.

## A) PRIMARY — plot-level prevalence of gardening-introduced species (denominator = ALL sampled plots in habitat)
| habitat | plots | occupied | % (Wilson 95% CI) | median elev | usable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wetlands | 38 | 19 | **50.0 (34.8–65.2)** | 148 | yes |
| Urban | 65 | 31 | **47.7 (36.0–59.6)** | 156 | yes |
| Coastal | 29 | 13 | **44.8 (28.4–62.5)** | 10 | yes |
| Riparian | 61 | 22 | **36.1 (25.2–48.6)** | 378 | yes |
| Croplands | 92 | 19 | 20.7 (13.6–30.0) | 382 | yes |
| Meadows | 39 | 3 | 7.7 (2.7–20.3) | 896 | yes |
| Coniferous forests | 77 | 5 | 6.5 (2.8–14.3) | 591 | yes |
| Broad-leaved forests | 68 | 3 | 4.4 (1.5–12.2) | 640 | shown, excluded from ranking (4 occurrence records) |
| Scrublands | 106 | 2 | 1.9 (0.5–6.6) | 502 | excluded (5 records) |
| Rock outcrops | 57 | 0 | 0.0 (0.0–6.3) | 990 | excluded (1 record) |

Overall 117/632 plots (18.5%) hold ≥1 gardening-introduced species; 191/632 (30.2%) hold any non-native.

## B) SECONDARY, explicitly separate — occurrence-conditioned views
sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total): Wetlands 55.8% (42–68), Coastal 53.5, Riparian 36.5, Meadows 30.8, Urban 29.8, Croplands 18.5; Coniferous forests 87.5 (7/8) and Broad-leaved forests 100 (4/4). **The two views are uncorrelated (Spearman rho = 0.08, p = 0.83).** Why they diverge, in one line: the forests top view B only because their denominators are 4 and 8 records (they host almost no unintentional/AgriForest colonisers), whereas view A counts against all 68/77 plots — tiny-n habitats versus the 441 zero-record plots drive the flip, so the two are never blended in the table.

## Formal test (2×10 plot-level occupancy, Monte-Carlo primary)
chi² = 139.45, df = 9 → **Monte-Carlo p ≤ 0.0001** (10,000 permutations, seed 20261023, 0 exceedances; independently reproduced with a different RNG stream at 20,000 permutations, p = 5e-5); asymptotic p = 1.3e-25; 0/20 expected cells < 5 (min 5.37). Plot-level std residuals: Urban +5.47, Wetlands +4.51, Coastal +3.29, Riparian +3.19, Croplands +0.48 | Meadows −1.57, Coniferous −2.45, Broad-leaved −2.70, Rock −3.25, Scrublands −3.98.

Robustness — direction preserved in every variant: ≥20-record habitats only (Coastal, Croplands, Riparian, Urban, Wetlands): chi² 17.34, perm p = 0.0020, top habitat unchanged; dropping the three uninformative habitats: chi² 55.86, perm p ≤ 0.0001.

## Descriptive only (marked NON-INFERENTIAL — species recur across plots/habitats)
10×3 occurrence std residuals for n.gard: Coniferous +2.50, Wetlands +2.51, Broad-leaved +2.19, Coastal +2.03 vs Croplands −2.91; AgriForest signal sits entirely in Riparian (+3.93). Nominal chi² 75.2 (df 18) but 17/30 expected cells < 5 (min 0.05), so this table is never used for a p-value.

## Sensitivity (proportionate, no full GLM build-out)
Effort rarefaction to 29 plots/habitat (5,000 draws): rank order identical to the raw ranking (Spearman rho = 1.00), so unequal sampling (29–106 plots) is not generating the pattern. Elevation is a genuine co-driver: occupancy 37.3% → 24.7% → 8.9% → 3.2% across elevation quartiles (rho = −0.368); habitat-vs-elevation logit LRTs: habitat alone p = 4.4e-22 (pseudo-R² 0.211), elevation alone p = 2.7e-18 (0.131), elevation added to habitat p = 1.3e-4. After elevation adjustment Wetlands/Urban/Coastal/Riparian retain 8–10× odds vs broad-leaved forest (p ≤ 0.004) while Coniferous forests collapse to null (logit 0.32, p = 0.68). Covariates corroborate propagule pressure: urban cover 1 km buffer rho = +0.375, distance to road rho = −0.192.

## Context (region-wide counts, NOT estimated from the 632 plots)
Species table: Gardening 42 rows / 42 unique species, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9 (4 duplicated=TRUE dual-pathway rows kept as-is, so pathway-specific species counts for those 4 species are not mutually exclusive). Mean habitat.range: AgriForest 1.56 < Gardening 1.95 < Unintentional 2.77. Temporal rise of gardening: 18 → 54 → 142 → 397 species (16.8% → 44.6% → 49.0% → 75.2% of each period's introductions). Phylogenetic tree: out of scope, untouched.

## FINAL HYPOTHESIS (all plot-level numbers are estimates from these 632 plots)
Prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants varies strongly and systematically by habitat type: it is highest in low-elevation, human-subsidised and hydric habitats — Wetlands (50.0% of plots) and Urban (47.7%), then Coastal (44.8%) and Riparian (36.1%) — intermediate in Croplands (20.7%), and lowest in upland semi-natural habitats, Coniferous/Broad-leaved forests and Meadows (≤7.7%) and effectively zero in Scrublands/Rock outcrops; the four lowland-disturbed habitats hold ~44% garden-occupied plots versus 6.0% in the forest/meadow set (risk difference 38.1 pp, 95% CI 30.3–45.9; risk ratio 7.4×; OR 12.4, 6.3–24.2). Habitat × pathway heterogeneity is significant beyond chance (permutation p ≤ 0.0001). Because gardening supplies ~75% of recent regional introductions while gardening species have narrower realised habitat ranges (1.95 vs 2.77 habitat types) than unintentional ones, we hypothesise this is propagule-pressure- and disturbance-mediated — largely, but not entirely, expressed through elevation and urban cover (both remain significant covariates; habitat keeps an independent elevation-adjusted effect) — predicting that garden-origin species will keep accumulating in urban/wetland/coastal/riparian plots while upland semi-natural habitats remain comparatively depauperate in garden introductions.

payload.hypothesis: Prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants varies strongly and systematically by habitat type in the Barcelona province plot network (632 plots): it is highest in low-elevation, human-subsidised and hydric habitats - Wetlands (50.0% of plots, 95% CI 34.8-65.2) and Urban (47.7%, 36.0-59.6), then Coastal (44.8%) and Riparian (36.1%) - intermediate in Croplands (20.7%), and lowest in upland semi-natural habitats, Coniferous forests (6.5%), Broad-leaved forests (4.4%) and Meadows (7.7%), with Scrublands (1.9%) and Rock outcrops (0%) too sparsely colonised to support a rate. The four lowland-disturbed habitats hold 44.0% garden-occupied plots (85/193) versus 6.0% (11/184) in the forest/meadow set - risk difference 38.1 percentage points (30.3-45.9), risk ratio 7.4x, odds ratio 12.4 (6.3-24.2), Fisher p = 9e-19 - and habitat x pathway heterogeneity in plot occupancy is significant beyond chance (chi2 = 139.4, df = 9, Monte-Carlo p <= 0.0001 with 10,000 permutations, seed 20261023; unchanged in direction under the >=20-record restriction, p = 0.002, and under effort rarefaction to 29 plots/habitat, rank rho = 1.00). Because the gardening pathway supplies ~75% of regional introductions in the most recent period (397 of 528 species; 18 -> 54 -> 142 -> 397 across periods) while gardening species occupy fewer habitat types (mean habitat.range 1.95) than unintentional ones (2.77), we hypothesise the habitat gradient is propagule-pressure and disturbance mediated - largely expressed through elevation (occupancy 37.3% in the lowest elevation quartile vs 3.2% in the highest; rho = -0.37) and urban cover within 1 km (rho = +0.38) - but with habitat retaining an independent effect after elevation adjustment (Wetlands/Urban/Coastal/Riparian 8-10x odds vs broad-leaved forest, all p <= 0.004). Prediction: garden-origin species will keep accumulating in urban, wetland, coastal and riparian plots while upland forest, meadow, scrub and rock habitats stay comparatively free of garden introductions.
payload.workflow: 1) Confirmed primary source: invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots x 37 cols; row = plot with 632 unique coordinate pairs; n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo = n.total in 632/632 rows); habitat identity is absent from invasion_success_pathways.csv (habitat.range is a count), so per-habitat species lists are not recoverable and were not approximated. 2) PRIMARY prevalence = fraction of all sampled plots per habitat with n.gard >= 1, with Wilson 95% CIs. 3) SECONDARY, reported separately and never blended: occurrence-conditioned share sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) per habitat, plus occupancy restricted to colonised plots; rank agreement between views quantified (Spearman rho = 0.08). 4) FORMAL TEST: 2 x 10 plot-level Gardening-occupied vs not table, primary p from 10,000-permutation Monte-Carlo chi-square (labels permuted across plots, seed 20261023), asymptotic chi-square reported alongside, plot-level standardised residuals for the gardening column. 5) ROBUSTNESS: restriction to habitats with >=20 occurrence records; exclusion of uninformative habitats (<=5 records); both compared for direction agreement. 6) DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: 10 x 3 occurrence standardised residuals, labelled non-inferential because species recur across plots. 7) SENSITIVITY: effort rarefaction to the smallest habitat sample (29 plots, 5,000 draws) and elevation checks (quartile occupancy, Spearman, and a small logistic comparison of habitat vs habitat+elevation LRTs, dropping perfectly separated habitats) - no full GLM. 8) CONTEXT (region-wide, not from the plots): pathway species counts and mean habitat.range from invasion_success_pathways.csv (4 duplicated=TRUE dual-pathway rows retained), and the temporal rise of the gardening pathway. 9) phylogenetic_tree.txt deliberately out of scope. 10) Validation: Wilson CIs recomputed with statsmodels, chi2 recomputed against scipy, permutation p reproduced on a second RNG stream (20,000 permutations), occupancy counts recomputed by an independent groupby.
